content: ## How to Link and Apply CONNECT This page will guide you through the process of linking inZOI with CONNECT and applying outfits. * * * ### Step 1: Signing Up and Linking CONNECT 1-1. Launch the game. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217241753) 1-2. Select **[Mods]** from the menu on the left side of the main screen. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209209625) 1-3. Click **[Add Mods]** at the top. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209210137) 1-4. Click the **[CONNECT]** card. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217245721) 1-5. After reviewing the Terms of Service and policies, select your preferred linking method to proceed. * If you click **[I agree]** : A temporary account will be created based on your Steam ID, allowing you to start immediately. * Even if you start with a temporary account, you can always link your Steam ID to a CONNECT account later via **[Join CONNECT]** in the profile menu. * If you click **[Sign in]** : You will log in and start with your CONNECT account, and your current Steam ID will be instantly linked to that account. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209213465) 1-6. Log in if you already have a CONNECT account, or create a new one if you don't. * If you already have a CONNECT account: Enter your email and password to **[Sign In]**. * If you are a new user: Click **[Sign up]** at the bottom to register for an account. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209218073) 1-8. Once you have logged in, return to the in-game CONNECT page and check the top right corner to verify that your account has been successfully linked. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217251097)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217252377) ### Step 2: Equipping Outfits 2-1. Click **[Back to inZOI]** in the top left corner to return to the game, ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209224473) 2-4. Click the **[Manage Mods]** tab to verify that the downloaded outfit has been successfully added to the **[Installed Mods]** list. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311209227417) 2-5. Click **[Back]** in the top left corner to return to the main screen. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217269273) 2-6. Select **[Character Studio]** on the main page. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217270041) 2-7. Select the **[Outfits]** category at the bottom. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/59311217273369) 2-8. title: Creating 3D Fabric
content: **Objective** Create a Fabric contents by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** When creating FABRIC file, please follow the rules below. **[Required]** * The fabric file format must be *zfab. * You must upload the thumbnail image. (For more information on thumbnail images, check out at #5 below.) * You must create a file by used for the fabric material according to the repeated image. * The size of the Maps used for fabric material must be 4K or less. **[Recommended]** * You should enter information in the Tag whether the pattern type is Solid or Pattern. * The product is only visible from the Render, so you should register the rendered image as a thumbnail. * You must enter the weight and thickness of the fabric in the Description. * You must enter the measurement information (whether the equipment is used, the name of the equipment, and the measurement institution) in the Description. * You must enter the fiber content of the fabric in Tag. (e.g., Cotton 100%, Cotton 97%, Spandex 3%) * You must enter information for the applied MAP. (TEXTURE, NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP) **※** Enter the product details for the convenience of CONNECT users. After carefully checking the contents below, click the NEXT button at the bottom to move on to the next steps. If there is any missing information, product registration may be rejected during the inspection stage. ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775510988953) **1\. DESCRIPTION (REQUIRED) ** 1-1. Enter the information of applied MAP. (Examples) TEXTURE. NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP (FUR) 1-2. If you are going to sell the actual products, enter the URL of the sales page. The link will automatically create when you enter the address attached as http or https. **2\. TAGS (REQUIRED)** This is where the search feature works. Entering the types of the selling products will help customers. 2-1. For fabric, you must enter the fiber content of the fabric. (Examples: Cotton100%, Cotton97%Spandex3%) (Examples) Write it without space. Cotton100% **or** Cotton97%Spandex3% 2-2. If you have registered Map on a fabric material, enter the information whether it is a solid or a pattern. (E.g., Solid, Pattern) (Examples) Solid **or** Pattern **3\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files related to fabric. However, it is impossible to track where the attached files from ATTACHMENT are being used. **4\. ADD SUB IMAGES** Additionally, register the image that shows the characteristics of the fabric well. For the actual products to be sold, you can register a real photo of the product. **5\. THUMBNAIL (REQUIRED)** Please register an image that clearly shows the texture and characteristics of the fabric. If a material visible only when render is applied, please register the rendered image. You may be rejected, If you upload a garment image as a fabric thumbnail.
content_description: This web page provides essential guidelines and requirements for creating and submitting fabric files using CLO and Marvelous Designer software, ensuring proper formatting and detailed descriptions for successful product registration.

CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description 1 **When uploading the items to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775525101849) **① UPLOAD (Mandatory)** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **② TITLE (Mandatory)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. Available on FV2 avatars **④ TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **⑤ ATTACHMENT** You may upload additional files by clicking the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button, and also able to select multiple files. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. Uploading multiple files as a compressed archive is not allowed. Each item must contain only a single file. (They cannot be downloaded from the CONNECT library, and buyers will not be able to view them in the viewer.) **※ Note:** The size of the upload item must be **less than 500 MB**. **⑥ ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally attach the SUB-IMAGES to highlight the item. Upload the files you would like to provide additionally by clicking the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button. **Supported image formats: *.jpg / *.jpeg / *.png** **⑦ THUMBNAIL** You may set or change the Thumbnail. Drag & Drop the thumbnail image into the **'THUMBNAIL BOX'** or click the **'CHOOSE FILE'** button to upload the image. Supported image formats: *.jpg / *.jpeg / *.png Recommended Thumbnail Size: 600 x 800(px) & ratio 3:4 **※ Note:** For the best search result, it is recommended to use English in the title, description, and tags of the item. ## ### 3\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description 2 ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775551984793) **① SET ITEM CATEGORIES** Detailed categories are provided based on the uploaded item's format, and you can select the specific category for their items in this section. Adding categories will significantly improve the item compatibility and search results. Users can search and filter items by category. **② SET COLLECTION** Users can decide the Collection to include their items. By default, items are assigned to the default collection. Customers can see the items in the assigned collection in their portfolio. **③ PRICING & LICENSE OPTIONS** Users can set the price and license options for their items: **Paid Item** : Select the **'Paid Item'** if you wish to sell the items. **※ Note:** CONNECT charges a **30%** commission on the item's sales. **Free Item** : Select **'Free Item'** to allow users to download their item for free. **※ Note:****Sellers cannot change a 'Free item' to a 'Paid item' after Publication.** **④ BASIC &EXTENDED LICENSE PRICE** Basic License Price: Enable to set the price for the basic license of the item. Extended License Price: Enable to set the price of the extended license 1 to 8 times the item's price. **⑤ PHYSICAL PRODUCTION** Sellers can allow physical production by clicking the **'Physical Production'** checkbox. ※ The following option will be limited if the original item is not allowed for physical production. **⑥ PUBLISH OPTIONS** Click the **'PUBLISH'** button to publish the item: **'PAID ITEM'** goes through review before publishing. It stays in **'DRAFT'** status until the review team approves. During the **'DRAFT'** status, creators can edit or re-upload the item. **'FREE ITEM'** will be published without any approval. Clicking the **'DRAFT'** button makes the item invisible to other users and allows you to either edit or re-upload. **⑦ BACK / UPLOAD** Click the **'BACK'** button to return to the previous step or the **'UPLOAD'** button to proceed to the next step. ### 4\. PREVIEW PAGE You can check whether the uploaded files and item information are correctly registered before publishing. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775542395033) **① ITEM STATUS** You can check the current status of the item. **'PAID ITEM'** will stay in **'DRAFT,'** hidden from other users, until the review team approves it. Upon approval, the status of the 'PAID ITEM' will change to 'PUBLISH.' **'FREE ITEM'** will be published without any approval. **② DELETE / EDIT** You can delete the uploaded files or item information by clicking the **'DELETE'** button. You can change the uploaded files or item information by clicking the **'EDIT'** button.

title: Seller Information Guide
content: ## **How to Register as a Seller Video** [](https://youtu.be/1U8VWlkk1Z4?si=SSxSHGhzcV1WvHbB) ## **Find Seller Information Here** 1) Select the profile image at the top right of the CONNECT page. ![1.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775555796121) 2) Select the Sales menu. ![2.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775513937689) 3) Select the INFO tab on the Sales page. ![3.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775498862105) ## **Enter Seller Info** 1) Press the CREATE button at the very bottom of the INFO page to start editing. ![4.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775498983705) 2) After accurately entering information for each item, select the seller type in the TAX INFORMATION section. * Non US seller (Individual): For individuals who are not corporations, including those who are not American or Americans who do not reside in the USA. * Non US seller (Entities): Corporations from countries other than the USA, including corporations established abroad by Americans. * US Seller: Americans who pay taxes in the USA, or American corporations. ![5.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775556278809) 3) Download the tax file according to the selected Type by clicking on the Download Link. ![6.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775556427673) 4) After completing the Tax document, press 'Choose File' to attach the file you have prepared. (Please refer to the [manual](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302175385) for how to complete the tax document). ![7.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775530810393) 5) Upon completing all required fields, finalize your submission by clicking the SUBMIT button. ![8.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775547067673) ## **Seller Info Submission Status** ### Pending * Once the Seller Info submission is complete, a status value of PENDING will appear at the top. * The information must be reviewed and approved by an administrator for the Seller Info registration to be finally completed. * The review process can take from 1 to a maximum of 10 business days. * During the Pending status, the information can be edited or updated. ![9-1.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775515096089) ### Rejected * This status indicates that the Seller Info has not been finally approved and has been rejected. * By clicking the message icon to the right of the REJECTED text, you can view the reasons for the rejection. * You can modify the Seller Info and resubmit it by pressing the SUBMIT button again. ![9-2.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775564088601) ### Confirmed * Your Seller Info registration has been finally approved. * If your earnings meet the CONNECT payment conditions, you can start receiving payments from the next scheduled payment date. * If you modify the information in the Confirmed status, it will revert to Pending, and the information will be reviewed again. * Earnings received during the review and approval process will be paid based on the previous information. (If you need to modify your information, it should be done before the 10th of each month.) ![9-3.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775515410329)
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to register as a seller, including step-by-step instructions for entering seller information, understanding submission statuses, and accessing essential resources.

title: Garment Tab
content: **1)****Polygon Optimization** **Objective** In the Garment Tab, adjust the Poly Count of the garment to match the platform you intend to export it to. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56585653092249) 1. You can manually input the desired Poly Count. 2. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims. * When the pattern’s mesh style is changed to Quad, it displays the total number of polygons, including the number of polygons changed to Quad and the remaining Triangles. * You can also check the polygon counts in the bottom left corner of the 3D window. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56585653093657) 3. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims, converted into Triangles. 4. It shows the Poly Count of the Avatar. 5. Optimize the garment mesh according to the input provided in #1. * If you enter a value smaller than the modifiable range, the value will be automatically adjusted and applied as the minimum value (variable). 6. It switches to the Mask Brush tool. The EveryWear window temporarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper-right corner of the 3D window. 7. Move to the Auto Seal tool. The EveryWear window will briefly close, and the Auto Seal tool will appear in the upper-right corner of the 3D window. **1-1) Applying Mask Brush** **Objective** Use the Mask Brush in the 3D and 2D windows to define the Mask area. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/49331558190873) 1. Switch tabs to set the surfaces where the Mask will be applied. * The Front and Back tab of the Mask Brush are based on the 2D pattern window, while in the 3D window, you can mask both sides. 2. Select a type to define how the area will be selected. (Brush / Box / Lasso) 3. You can select a mode to either add or subtract from the mask area. 4. Adjust the size of the Mask Brush. 5. When this option is enabled, all closed area that includes the selected point will be masked. ※ This option is only available when the Type is set to Brush. 6. When this option is enabled, you can work on both the front and back sides simultaneously. 7. Clear all applied masks. 8. Mode, Size, Select Enclosed Region and Double-Sided Brush settings will be reset. 9. The Mask Brush window will close, and the EveryWear window will open. **1-2) Auto Seal** **Objective** The Auto Seal feature is used to close the holes inside the garment, preventing the interior from being visible. * This feature helps close open areas of the garment, such as sleeves or hems, preventing the inner side from appearing empty. * By closing these holes, you can prevent the inner side of the garment from being exposed when the avatar moves, resulting in a more polished final look. * Enclosed or hidden mesh is automatically masked to optimize performance and prevent the use of unnecessary geometry. **Details** **![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56585700816153)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775689910169)** 1. Click the Auto Seal button. 2. Create Guidelines. \- Disc Mode: Create a disc by placing three points on the pattern. The curve (or path) cut by this disc becomes the guideline. \- 3D Pen Mode: Draw a curve (or path) on the garment to create the guideline (similar to the previous 3P Pen). Align the last point with the first point to complete the curve (or path). 3. Select Hidden Areas. \- Select the direction in which the face should be created, then apply ‘Auto Seal.’ ※ Note : Auto Seal is only activated in 3D view when the Rendering Mode is set to Thick. **2) Rigging** **Objective** Rigging the garments to the avatar. * Rigging is a fundamental aspect of 3D process, creating a skeleton structure with joints and bones to enable animations for 3D models. * EveryWear's rigging merges the outfit with the avatar's joints, allowing them to move together. * This rigging process also involves weight painting, which determines how much each part of the outfit is influenced by the movement of the avatar’s joints. This rigging process involves setting up and creating the controllable structure for the movement of the avatar and the outfit. * CLO and Marvelous Designer specialize in detailed and realistic clothing animations through advanced garment simulations. However, for gaming purposes, the considerable data size of simulation-based clothing animations may not always be efficient. * Therefore, EveryWear optimizes by utilizing Rigging instead of simulations to effectively synchronize the movements of outfits and avatars, prioritizing efficiency. * Starting from version 2024.2 of CLO and Marvelous Designer, the accuracy of Auto-rigging has been further improved. * Starting from version 2026.0 of CLO and Marvelous Designer, the new Rig Template feature is now avaiable. This feature is particularly effective for creating garments like skirts that require precise movement or unique handling relative to the avatar’s skeletal structure. **2-1) Rig Method - Transfer Weights** **Objective** * Rigging the garments to the avatar. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56585653097369) 1. Clothing is automatically rigged to the avatar. * When rigging is applied, the ‘Update’ and ‘Brush tools’ will appear as shown in <Image2> * If the avatar does not have joints or if there are multiple avatars within the same project, rigging will not proceed. * When attempting to simulate the garment in the rigging state, the following warning message will be displayed. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775739338009) 1. * Yes : The rigging information will be deleted as soon as the costume is simulated, and the rigging menu returns to its initial state. * No : The simulation will not proceed, and the existing rigging information will be maintained. * 1-1. All Patterns: Updates the rigging for all patterns, regardless of the current pattern selection. * 1-2. Selected Patterns: Updates the rigging only for the currently selected pattern(s). 2. Target Joint : Used to exclude or remove specific joint weights from the rigging target. \- If the rigging has already been applied: After setting the Target Joint, click Update to remove all weights applied to that joint. 3. All Patterns: Rigs/updates all patterns. 4. Selected Patterns: Rigs/updates only the selected patterns. 1. Tip: When rigging for the first time, use All Patterns to process all patterns. For partial edits, use the Selected Patterns option. 2. Tip: After checking Selected Patterns, click Update to re-rig only the selected patterns. 5. Show Avatar Joints : Displays the avatar’s joint points in the 3D window. 6. Max Influence Joints : Set the maximum number of joints that can affect each vertex. 7. Switch to Bind Pose : Returns the avatar to its original pose defined during creation. \- It is independent of the loading pose or the most recent pose. \- If switched to Bind Pose when rigging is not applied, the current draping state may be altered. **\- Notes** \- It is recommended to perform rigging in the Bind Pose state. \- If rigging is performed in a non-Bind Pose state, artifacts may occur when editing weights. 8. Re-rig based on the current state of the garment. 9. Navigate to the Brush tool. The EveryWear window momentarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper right corner of the 3D window. **2-2) Rig Method - Template** **Objective** * This feature aims to automate the creation and skinning of garment-specific joints to resolve issues such as silhouette distortion and mesh collapsing that occur when rigging wide garments directly to avatar joints. * By selecting a rigging template optimized for specific pattern characteristics and generating dedicated joints, users can efficiently achieve natural movement for garments requiring specialized handling, such as skirts and capes. * Recommended Garment Types: Skirts, capes, hems of long coats and jackets, wide sleeves of traditional costumes, neckties, ribbons, mufflers, etc. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56585700818073) **Details** * Creating Joints on Selected Patterns Precautions *Please ensure that the rigging process is performed in the [Transfer Weights] tab before using this feature. 1\. Select Rig Method: Set to [Template]. 2\. Select Target Patterns: Select the patterns to which joint generation or rigging will be applied. 3\. Set Template Type: Select the type (ex: Skirt) from the [Template Type] tab. 4\. Adjust Detailed Options: Configure specific parameters according to the selected template type. * skirt rib count: Sets the total number of bones (ribs) to be placed along the circumference of the skirt. A higher count allows for more precise control over the horizontal movement of the skirt. * joint count per rib: Sets the number of joints that make up each individual bone (rib). A higher number of segments results in smoother, more natural curvature when the skirt bends. * fitting strength: Adjusts the degree to which the generated bones adhere to the avatar's movement. A higher value causes the bones to more sensitively reflect the avatar's motions. 5\. Execute Joint Generation: Click ‘Create Joints on Selected Patterns’ to generate the joints. You can verify the generated joints by enabling ‘Show Avatar Joints (Shift+X).’ 6\. Apply Rigging: Select ‘Apply’ located to the right of the Rigging button. 7\. Complete Skinning: When the notification window appears, select ‘Proceed’ to complete the final skinning process. **3) Brush_Weight** **Objective** Modify the weight value using the brush. * Weight Painting ensures the rigged outfit moves seamlessly with the avatar's motions. * Weight Painting adjusts joint influence on surrounding vertices for natural and fluid movements. * While EveryWear auto-distributes weights based on the avatar, it's essential to check for any outfit penetration or inaccuracies in motion. Make necessary weight adjustments if needed. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927157285273) 1. Set the Brush to Weight Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) 2. Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) * Add : Add / Increase the weight value. * Subtract : Subtract / Decreases the weight value. * Smooth : Adjusts the weight value to match the surrounding areas. 3. Set Brush properties. * Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. (Hotkey : Alt + [ , ] ) * Size : Change the size of the brush. (Hotkey : [ , ] ) * Focal : Adjust the intensity difference between the center and edge of the brush. * Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. 4. Initialize the Brush property value. 5. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. **3-1)****Applying Weight Brush** * After selecting the Avatar's Joint, users can adjust Weight value by using a brush to add or subtract. * Real-time Weight adjustments in 2D window are possible as well. * **Add Weight** * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Add. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Add Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value increases, it will be represented with a deeper red color. * **Subtract Weight** * 1.Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Subtract. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Subtract Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value decreases, it will be represented with a deeper blue color. When the Weight value is 0, no weight color information will be displayed. * **Smooth (Single Joint)** * This function smooths the Joint weight of vertices based on the selected joint, softly adjusting the weight differences with surrounding vertices. * The sum of the joint weights for each vertex is always maintained at 1, and when the weight of the selected joint for a vertex is adjusted, the weights of the remaining joints are automatically scaled to maintain balance. However, if the weight of the selected joint is not different from that of surrounding vertices, no smoothing will occur. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Single Joint). * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 6\. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. * Tips By applying the 'Full Smooth' function to the selected joint's skin weight, you can evenly smooth across the entire selected joint with one click, eliminating the need for manually painting weight with the Smooth brush. * Usage: Click on the joint you want to modify to view its weight, then press Ctrl+Shift and click on the selected joint again. You can adjust the smoothing strength by modifying the 'strength' parameter under brush properties. * **Smooth (Multiple Joints)** * It operates for all joints, smoothing the joint weights of each vertex along with the weights of surrounding vertices. * This is similar to selecting and using all joints in the Single Brush. In this process, the joint weights of each vertex are adjusted smoothly and simultaneously, while the sum of the joint weights for each vertex always remains 1. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Multiple Joints). * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. * **Joint Lock** * The Joint Lock feature is designed to influence only specific areas when modifying weights in situations such as the following: * When adjusting the weight value without affecting the selected joint. * When unrelated joints are causing the weight issues and need corrections (e.g., armpits, corners, sleeves, skirts, etc.). * When intricate weight adjustments are required for complex models. * Locked Joints will remain unaffected when adjusting other joints’ weight values. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Lock the Joint: Hold down Alt and click on the Joint. The Locked Joint will be highlighted in red. * To apply Lock to all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. * 4\. Unlock the Joint: To unlock, Hold Alt and click on the locked Joint again. Once unlocked, the Joint will be displayed in white. * To unlock all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. * **Hammering** * Hammering is a feature that automatically adjusts the weight values of a specific vertex to closely match the surrounding weight values when there is a significant disparity. * This feature comes in handy in situations where certain areas, like armpits, the bottom of pants, sleeves, and so on, are unintentionally affected by unwanted joints, resulting in awkward deformations or the strange spikes. * 1\. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. * 3\. Select Joint: Hold down Ctrl and click on the joint. The selected joint will be highlighted in yellow. * 4\. Hammering: Hold down Shift and click on the desired vertex. When Shift is pressed, the mouse cursor changes from the brush shape to a red dot, indicating that it can recognize vertices. * **Copy Symmetric Weights** * This function allows you to copy the weight values from one side of a symmetric pattern to the opposite side. * By editing only one side and applying the same values to the other, you can reduce the time spent on weight adjustments. * 1\. Switch to Weight Brush mode. (Make sure no joints are selected.) * 2\. Select the pattern(s) whose weight values you want to copy. (Selection is possible in the 2D or 3D view.) * If multiple patterns are selected, the weight values of each pattern will be copied. * If both symmetric patterns are selected, the copy operation will not be performed. * 3\. Right Click → Copy Symmetric Weights to copy the weight values to the opposite symmetric pattern. * The joint-specific weight values applied to each pattern can be checked by selecting the corresponding joint. **4) Brush_Sculpt** **Objective** Use the Brush to modify the shape of the garment. **Details** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51927157286297) 1. Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) 2. Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) * Grab : Use this mode to grab and reshape the 3D clothing surface. * Smooth : Use this mode to make the 3D clothing surface smoother. * Fix Intersection : Use this mode to correct areas where intersections occur between the garment and the avatar or between the surfaces of the garment. 3. Set Brush properties. * Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. ( Hotkey : Ctrl + [ , ] ) * Size : Change the size of the brush. ( Hotkey : [ , ] ) * Focal : Adjust the difference between the brush center and edge intensity values. * Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. 4. Initialize the Brush property value. 5. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. **4-1)****Applying****Sculpt****Brush** * Using the Sculpt Brush allows users to modify the shape of the garment. * **Applying Grab Brush** * Utilize this brush when the garment penetrates inside the avatar or when garment layers overlap, causing visibility issues. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Grab. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Grab Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the selected area will move along with the mouse. Note that the Weight value will not have any effect. * **Applying Smooth Brush** * Utilize this brush to create a smoother surface for garments or to soften angular areas while modeling. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Smooth. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Smooth Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the surface will be smoothed based on its surroundings * **Applying Fix Intersection Brush** * Utilize this brush for areas where the garment intersects with the avatar or where garments overlap, as other existing brushes may struggle with these areas. * 1\. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. * 2\. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. * 3\. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Fix Intersection. * 4\. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. * 5\. Apply Fix Intersection Brush : Apply the brush to the desired area to automatically correct intersections where the avatar or garments overlap.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for optimizing garment polygon counts, applying mask brushes, and rigging techniques in 3D garment design for enhanced performance and realistic animations.

title: Tips & best practices
content: * You can reset CLO/MD LiveSync Editor by closing the active instance of the Editor, then reopening it. * Due to how CLO and Marvelous Designer behave, they can be unresponsive when it is processing a big amount of data. Such situation is as the following: * Right after hitting Update button * The very first update routine may take a while, but subsequent update requests will be faster. * Right after hitting Save to Geometry Cache button * CLO and Marvelous Designer will be unresponsive for a while, and there will be a pop-up window in the CLO/MD LiveSync Editor once CLO and Marvelous Designer finishes sending animation data to Unreal. Try not to press the button multiple times in a row, otherwise unexpected crashes may happen. * As garment data is detailed and can be heavy, putting in multiple garment assets (Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh, or Geometry Cache) in a world may result in reduced performance in terms of FPS. * For Static Mesh, Nanite can be a great choice and it is compatible with Static Mesh version of imported garment. Details about Nanite can be found in the following link: [Nanite Virtualized Geometry](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine/) * Our default way of expressing transparent garment is dithered opacity (see [a reference YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ieHpTG_P8Q0&ab_channel=TechArtAid)). This method may result in fine noises on mesh surfaces due to its characteristics. If **Order Independent Translucency** option is enabled, it is possible to make meshes without the surface noises by altering a property of a desired material. * Open up a desired material, and change its **Blend Mode** to **Translucent**. ![000.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775814063769) * Occasionally LiveSync usage may yield the following error regarding lack of memory, which leads to a crash issue. In this case, if you separate an avatar and garment into more than 2 ZPRJ files from a single ZPRJ file, sending the avatar and garment separately may resolve the crash issue temporarily. ![Untitled \(4\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775797400217)
content_description: This web page provides essential troubleshooting tips and performance optimization strategies for effectively using the CLO/MD LiveSync Editor with Unreal Engine, ensuring a smoother experience when managing garment assets.

title: MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync
content: Please note that this feature is _experimental_. You can bring your own MetaHuman to CLO and Marvelous Designer for fitting garments: * Create your own MetaHuman or download preset MetaHuman into Unreal Editor. You can follow the official MetaHuman setup & guide provided by Epic Games: [Getting Started with MetaHumans in Unreal Engine](https://docs.metahuman.unrealengine.com/en-US/metahumans-unreal-engine/getting-started/) Once MetaHuman is successfully imported in Unreal Editor, create an IK Retargeter asset. ![Untitled \(1\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775751131929) Then, create a source IK Rig. ![Untitled \(3\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775767823001) Once the source IK Rig is created, a target IK Rig can be set. MetaHuman Retargeter sample can be seen in the image below. ![Untitled \(4\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775760920217)![Untitled \(5\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775761160089) Open Animation Editor ([Unreal Animation Editor](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/animation-sequence-editor-in-unreal-engine/)). ![Untitled \(6\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775752614169) For the target MetaHuman, there are 2 sets of data within Animation Editor (see 1 and 2 in the image above): 1. a list of animation assets that can be applied to MetaHuman 2. components of MetaHuman (it is set automatically) In the 1st set of data, you can select an animation asset to export, then add or remove Collection to be exported in the 2nd set of data. ⚠️ **Please note** ⚠️: _Skeletal Mesh corresponding to a body must be placed at the top of the Skeletal Mesh section of “Additional Meshes”, which can be seen in ‘2’ of the image above (f_med_unw_body is at the top, while other Skeletal Meshes such as Bernice_FaceMesh is placed under the body mesh in terms of order)._ Pressing LiveSync button in the top toolbar brings out a context menu:![Untitled \(7\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775768999193) ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775771345689) Selecting Skeleltal Mesh shows Export Dialog as the following: ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775778950553) At the moment, the Ref Skeleton option is disabled, thus, it can be disregarded. After pressing Export button, it can be observed that MetaHuman Skeletal Mesh with animation is successfully imported in CLO or Marvelous Designer. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775803777817) Garments can be fit on the imported MetaHuman, and the results can be simply sent to CLO/MD LiveSync Editor using Update. Please note that you cannot save/export imported MetaHuman as different file formats other than ZPRJ in CLO/Marvelous Designer.

title: Opening CLO/MD LiveSync Editor
content: ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775577234073) Navigate to CLO/MD Live Sync Editor by going to **Window > CLO/MD LiveSync Editor**. When opening Live Sync Editor for the first time, you may get a warning pop-up window saying **Missing Project Settings**. Simply click **Enable Missing** , then click **Restart Now** in the second pop-up window. Then your Unreal Project will restart, and LiveSync becomes ready to be used. We highly recommend you to create a new Unreal project when starting with LiveSync, as LiveSync requires a couple of experimental features to be enabled, which may conflict with assets if LiveSync is added to existing projects. Note that **[asset migration](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/migrating-assets-in-unreal-engine/)** can be utilized to bring assets from another project into a new project. Unreal Engine features and assets requiring DirectX 12 is not fully compatible with LiveSync at the moment. ![Untitled.jpeg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775570644633)

title: Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor
content: ![update 버튼 위치.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775710001049) ![save 버튼 위치.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775710220697) There are 2 major features in the toolbar of CLO/MD LiveSync Editor, **Update** and **Save** : **Update** : The update button (CLO Virtual Fashion logo) allows users to instantly bring garment and avatar into CLO/MD LiveSync Editor. * Note that you can delete loaded garment and/or avatar by selecting “Garment” and/or “Avatar” in a selection tree in the left side of the editor screen, then hitting a Delete key. * Make sure that _simulation and animation has been turned off in CLO and Marvelous Designer_ , and set in either **Simulation mode** or **UV Editor mode** when attempting to press Update button. * In order to utilize Unified Material option embedded in ellipsis next to Update button, make sure that UV maps are arranged without overlapping with each other. UV maps can be manually arranged, or automatically arranged with [Auto UV Packing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053418574-UV-Editor-Mode)/[UV Packing](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037029912-UV-EDITOR-MODE-Edit-UV-location). Texture resolution is supported up to 8K. Unified Material option can be particularly useful when Puckering is applied to garment, or multiple Trim objects are present. Otherwise, the option can be turned off. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775725580697) Incorrect UV mapping for Unified Material: maps are placed on texture boundary lines ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775742811545) An example of maps being placed correctly, using UV Packing feature **Save** : Once garment and avatar are sent to CLO/MD LiveSync Editor, they can be saved as Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh, Geometry Cache or Animation Sequence depending on users' needs. After selecting a desired asset in LiveSync tree, it can be saved as one of four aforementioned Unreal Engine assets. Pressing Save button automatically disables target asset options that CLO/MD LiveSync Editor cannot save based on source data in CLO and Marvelous Designer (e.g. no animation in CLO or Marvelous Designer means that assets cannot be saved as Geometry Cache). ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775743146777) **![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775711509401)** **GC Material Combiner****(new feature in LiveSync 1.1.5)** : GC Material Combiner can be launched by navigating to LiveSync Editor > Tools > GCMaterialCombiner. This tool aims to help users with managing materials of multiple Geometry Cache assets. **Base Geometry Cache** slot takes a single Geometry Cache asset which will be used as a reference. Multiple Geometry Cache assets can be added under **Target Geometry Caches** slot. As long as the number of material slots for given Geometry Cache assets is same, material of Base Geometry Cache will be applied to all Geometry Cache assets listed in Target Geometry Caches. You can choose to delete 'unused/duplicate' materials by enabling **Delete all Other Materials** checkbox. Then materials for Target Geometry Caches will be deleted accordingly.

title: [Experimental] Expressing Fur in Unreal Engine via LiveSync
content: **This feature is available from CLO LiveSync 1.1.0.** Note that this is only available in CLO at the moment, and it will be supported in Marvelous Designer as render only fabrics are implemented in Marvelous Designer. This feature may result in unexpected crashes due to high memory usage of displaying Fur in Unreal Engine. ### Saving garments with Fur as Static Mesh ![fur-clo.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775841653145) First, assign Fur to desired Fabric(s), and apply the Fabric(s) to your garment. Then simply use Update feature to seamlessly bring garments to LiveSync Editor. The results can be saved as Static Mesh, and it can be observed that a Groom Asset is generated along with a Static Mesh. ![fur-ue-groomasset.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775808391449) Locate a Static Mesh asset in Outliner, and click on it to add a child component by clicking the Add button and selecting Groom Component. ![fur-ue-detail-groomcomponent.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775776475545) Once a Groom Component is added as a child component of a Static Mesh for your garments, a correct Groom Asset can be assigned to it. You can either drag a desired Groom Asset from Content Browser, or search for it by clicking on Groom Asset section in Details panel. ❗Please note that a Binding Asset needs to be created for Grooms. Details can be found in [**the official documentation for Setting Up Bindings for Grooms**](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/setting-up-bindings-for-grooms-in-unreal-engine). For more information on how to edit your Groom Asset, you can check out **[the official Groom Asset Editor User Guide on Epic Developer Community](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/groom-asset-editor-user-guide-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.3)**. ![fur-ue-groomcomponent-choose.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775842319257) ![fur-ue-staticmesh-result.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775777003033) ### Saving animated garments with Fur as Geometry Cache The setup for Geometry Cache is almost identical, and it only requires one additional step. For Geometry Cache, an additional Groom Binding asset is created. In a desired Geometry Cache asset, add a Groom Component as a child component, and assign a Groom Asset and a Groom Binding Asset to it. Keep in mind that this feature is experimental, and a Geometry Cache asset containing Fur information may result in a crash issue. ![fur-ue-geomcache-setup.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775809177625) ### Applying Simulation to Imported Fur Physics simulation can be applied on Groom Assets. For more information, please take a look at the official guide for Enabling [Physics Simulation on Grooms](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/enabling-physics-simulation-on-grooms-in-unreal-engine). Note that enabling physics simulation can result in reduced performance or unexpected crash issues. ![fur-ue-fur-simulation.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775843248153)

title: [Updated] MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync
content: Please note that this guide is based on **_[Skill up: CLO LiveSync for Unreal Engine](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_iO8Ob-5GHw&ab_channel=CLO)_**. LiveSync 1 is utilized in the video, but the overall workflow is identical outside the fundamental difference between LiveSync 1 and LiveSync 2. The MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync is inteded to work well with Sequencer, where you can animate your MetaHuman using control rigs. ### **1\. Download MetaHumans to Unreal Engine** You can follow this documentation: _**[Downloading MetaHumans](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/metahuman/downloading-metahumans-with-quixel-bridge)**_. ![MHC - get rid of clothes.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678547593753) Make sure to remove Tops and Bottoms in MetaHuman Creator before downloading it to Unreal Engine. ### **2\. Add Level Sequence and attach a MetaHuman to it** ![LiveSync - MHworkflow - Level Sequencer.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678536168217) You can add Level Sequence by navigating to the menu shown in the image above. The downloaded MetaHuman from the previous step can be added to the scene by locating the Blueprint for the MetaHuman and dragging it to the scene. In this example, Kellan is used. Then the MetaHuman can be added to a created Sequencer by: * Locating the Add button on the left hand side and navigating to Actor To Sequencer menu. * Locating the spawned Actor in Outliner and dragging it directly into the opened Sequencer tab. ![LiveSync - MHworkflow - Level Sequencer 4.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678547594649) After adding the MetaHuman to Sequencer, you can animate it with Control Rig in Sequencer. For more information, the following documentations elaborate on the process: * _**[Using MetaHumans in Sequencer](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/metahuman/using-metahumans-in-sequencer-in-unreal-engine)**_ * _**[Animating MetaHumans with Control Rig](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/metahuman/animating-metahumans-with-control-rig-in-unreal-engine)**_ ### **3\. Create Linked Animation Sequence and prepare it for export** ![LiveSync - MHworkflow - Level Sequencer 5.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678547595673) You can right click on the Body and select **Create Linked Animation Sequence** , which creates For the Animation Sequence Options pop-up window, you do not have to modify any settings. Proceed to next step by clicking Export to Animation. ![MH Animation - 1.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678536170393) After locating the Animation Sequence asset, you can double click it to open up Animation Editor. Before sending an animated MetaHuman body to CLO or Marvelous Designer, there are several important settings to be checked: **Preview Scene Settings**(the menu on the right-hand side) 1. **Mesh > Preview Mesh (Animation) **: The correct Skeletal Mesh must be selected. Please do not select a Skeletal Mesh with a '_preview' suffix. 2. **Additional Meshes > Skeletal Meshes **: Please select a Skeletal Mesh for a matching face mesh, otherwise there is no head part for a MetaHuman to be sent to CLO or Marvelous Designer. **Other options**(located in the center and the top of the editor) 1. 1. **Post process Animation Blueprint** : You can choose to enable it or disable it, based on the type of animation to be sent via LiveSync. With an incorrect setting here, you may experience issues like garment penetration as mesh deformation for the MetaHuman in Unreal Engine and CLO or Marvelous Designer will not match. **Please enable it for the Geometry Cache option, and disable it for the Skeletal Mesh option**. 2. **Skeletal Mesh** vs. **Geometry Cache** : Animation for MetaHuman can be sent to CLO or Marvelous Designer via LiveSync in either form: * LiveSync > as LiveSync > **Skeletal Mesh** : Joint animation is used for this asset type. This is lighter than the Geometery Cache type, however, it does not utilize blend shapes for MetaHumans. We aim to implement additional features around the Skeletal Mesh asset type in near future. * LiveSync > as LiveSync > **Geometry Cache** : Blend shapes for MetaHumans are taken into consideration for this asset type. For example, when bending an arm of a MetaHuman, the forearm and bicep regions close to the joint will be deformed together instead of the meshes simply clipping into each other. This method is generally a lot heavier than the Skeletal Mesh method, however, you can achieve more realistic results For the Skeletal Mesh asset type, please make sure to **Disable Post Process Blueprint** by navigating to a Blueprint for the MetaHuman, locating the Body component, and finding the option under the Animation section. Otherwise the body mesh for the MetaHuman in Unreal Engine might clip through the recorded garment animation from CLO or Marvelous Designer, as the MetaHuman would deform with blend shapes in consideration while the recorded garment animation would be based on the MetaHuman without blend shapes. ![MH - disablePostProcessBlueprint.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678547598233) ### **4\. Apply a garment to the imported MetaHuman body, record animation and use LiveSync to send the garment animation to Unreal Engine** ![mceclip0.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678536171161) Locate the imported MetaHuman in CLO or Marvelous Designer, then you can apply a garment to it. It can be simulated and recorded, and the result can be sent to Unreal Engine using LiveSync. Make sure to enable the **Include Cache Animation** option under the Garment section of the CLO/MD LiveSync mode for **Update** and **Save**. Then, you can locate the generated Geometry Cache asset for the garment and bring it in the scene. Once it is in the scene, add it to the Sequencer like the same way you added the MetaHuman to the Sequencer earlier. A Geometry Cache track can be attached to it by click on the plus button, and selecting Geometry Cache. ![MH animation - 2.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/46678547599385) That's all! You can also animate MetaHumans by utilizing Animation Retargeting in Unreal Engine. For more information, please check out _**[the official documentation on Animation Retargeting](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/animation-retargeting-in-unreal-engine)**_.

title: Opening CLO/MD LiveSync Mode
content: ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775630951065) Enable CLO/MD LiveSync Mode by navigating to **Selection Mode > CLO/MD LiveSync (Shift+9)**. Instead of a separate editor, a CLO/MD LiveSync tab will appear. You can control various options in the tab. ![opening LiveSync mode.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/53009661676313) The tab consists of the following components and options: 1. **Tab type** : The **LiveSync** tab is enabled by default. In the **Extensions** tab, there is a new feature called **Material Combiner**. 2. **Action buttons** : You can perform 3 actions in the LiveSync tab. * **Update** : Clicking on this button brings objects in CLO or Marvelous Designer based on import options under the Garment, Avatar, Scene and Props, and Override Transparent BlendMode sections. * **Save** : The imported asset is saved to a designated folder in the Content Browser, based on the save configurations under **Garment** , **Avatar** , **Scene and Props** , and **Override Transparent Blend Mode**. * **AsCloth** : Garments can be saved as a Chaos Cloth Asset. You must enable the **Include Garment Simulation Data** option to use this feature. For more details about the Chaos Cloth pipeline, you can check out the following manuals: * [Chaos Panel Cloth - Editor Walkthrough and Updates (5.4)](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/Mpze/unreal-engine-panel-cloth-editor-walkthrough-updates-5-4) * [Chaos Panel Cloth - Dataflow and Collision Updates (5.4)](Chaos%20Panel%20Cloth%20-%20Dataflow%20and%20Collision%20Updates%20\(5.4\)) * [Panel Cloth Example Files (5.4)](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/Ybvo/unreal-engine-panel-cloth-example-files-5-4) * [Panel Cloth Editor Updates (5.5)](https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/tutorials/xjpO/unreal-engine-panel-cloth-editor-updates-5-5) 3. **LiveSync Connection Status** : Either a green or a red circle will appear based on the connection status with CLO or Marvelous Designer. If it shows a red circle, you can check if you are using a compatible version, or perform simple actions in CLO or Marvelous Designer such as clicking on a pattern. Otherwise, please restart CLO or Marvelous Dseigner. 4. **Garment** * **Include Garment** : Enabling this option brings garments from CLO or Marvelous Designer to Unreal Engine. * **Single Object** vs. **Multiple Object** : You can choose either option to weld the meshes or keep them separate. * **Thin** vs. **Thick** : The Thin option corresponds to Textured Surface mode, while the Thick option corresponds to Thick Texture Surface mode in CLO and Marvelous Designer. * **Unified UV Coordinate** : The unified UV coordinates option is enabled when this option is checked. * **Include Garment Simulation Data** : This option is identical to the one in the USD Exporter of CLO and Marvleous Designer. Enabling this option is a prerequisite to saving a garment as a Chaos Cloth Asset mentioned above. * **Include Cache Animation** : If there is an animation in CLO or Marvelous Designer, you can enable this option to bring animated garment data to Unreal Engine. It can be saved as a Geometry Cache Asset. 5. **Avatar** * **Include Avatar** : Enabling this option brings avatars from CLO or Marvelous Designer to Unreal Engine. Please note that avatars with joints will be saved as Skeletal Mesh Assets by default. * **Avatar Animation** : Two options are exposed upon enabling this option, **Joint** and **Cache** animation. 6. **Scene and Props** * **Include Scene and Props** : This option allows you to control the LiveSync behavior for bringing in any Scene and Props objects from CLO or Marvelous Designer into Unreal Engine. 7. **Animation (✨Introduced in CLO/MD LiveSync 2.2.0)** * **Play Region** vs.**Entire Region** : Play Region uses Start & End Frame values from the Animation Editor in CLO or Marvelous Designer, while Entire Region uses the full animation. * **Bake Joint Animation Frames on FPS Mismatch** : **** Enabling this option resolves FPS discrepancies (e.g., loading a 30 FPS CLO animation into the 60 FPS Animation Editor) by baking joint animation data for intermediate, empty frames, ensuring the avatar animation sent via LiveSync to Unreal Engine is always identical to the source.) 8. **Override Transparent Blend Mode** * **Translucent** vs. **Opacity Mask** : You can choose Material Blend Modes for materials of garments being created via LiveSync. For more details about both modes, please check out [the Unreal Enigne documentation on Material Blende Modes](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/material-blend-modes-in-unreal-engine). 9. **Override Normal Texture Option (✨Introduced in CLO/MD LiveSync 2.2.0)** * **Flip Green Channel** : Enabling this option flips green channel for all normal maps of garments via CLO/MD LiveSync Mode.**** 10. **Combine Material (Material Combiner)** * This is an upgraded version of 'GC Material Combiner' introduced in LiveSync 1.1.5. You can use it with Static Mesh Assets as well as Geometry Cache Assets. 11. **Combine Pose (Pose Combiner)** * (Introduced in LiveSync 2.1.0) You can select a desired start pose and a target animation, then combine them with a transition duration to make it easier to apply garments to a MetaHuman in CLO or Marvelous Designer. For example, if the target animation is a running motion, it can be challenging to dress the MetaHuman directly. By choosing a simple A-pose as the start pose, you can now easily apply clothing before transitioning into the running animation.

title: Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Mode
content: ## **Update** ![LiveSync - update.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775647232921) Using LiveSync 2 is easier than LiveSync 1, because it is now available as an editor mode instead of a separate editor window. This allows you to seamlessly work on a scene without having to switch back and forth to the previous LiveSync Editor. You can press **Update** in CLO/MD LiveSync Mode, then assets from CLO or Marvelous Designer will be created as an **UsdStageActor** in the viewport. We are utilizing UsdStageActor and the USD importer in Unreal Engine because we believe that USD format is the future for all 3D applications. Significant improvements have been made in CLO and Marvelous Designer for exporting assets to USD files. From this moment, you can press the **Update** button whenever you want to bring updated assets from CLO or Marvelous Designer into Unreal Engine, and the UsdStageActor placed in the viewport will be updated accordingly. ## **Save** ![LiveSync - save prompt window.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775663975961) When you are done selecting save options and ready to save the assets to Unreal Engine assets, simply click on the **Save** button. Then a pop-up window for selecting the assets will show up. In the designated directory, the assets will be saved under a parent folder with its name mathcing a project file in CLO or Marvelous Designer. If a project file in CLO or Marvelous has never been saved, the parent folder in Unreal Engine will become 'Untitled'. ![LiveSync - save location and name.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775656378137) When you are done with the **Update** process, you can simply delete the UsdStageActor in the viewport. ## **AsCloth** As the Chaos Cloth workflow is designed to be used with MetaHumans, we recommend you to start with one of 18 available MetaHuman body types in the Library of CLO and Marvelous Designer. They can be located by navigating to Avatar > Avatar > MetaHuman. Please check out [a tutorial video about the Chaos Cloth workflow for Marvelous Designer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nf6OUDoPCPs&ab_channel=MarvelousDesigner) (and this is identical for CLO).

title: Tips & Tricks
content:
This guide provides the basic instructions required for the work, along with various examples of modifications. Please refer to the following content and apply it to your work according to each garment’s specific situation. * * * ### **Case #1. Adjusting Garment Length** Please refer to the length guidelines on the template avatar, making sure skirts sit above the knee and sleeves do not cover the back of the hand. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345796121) * * * ### **Case #2. How to illustrate Torn Areas** When illustrating torn areas using internal lines, the topology does not smoothly transition, and the appearance looks unnatural. In these cases, using textures instead of creating separate patterns is strongly recommended, as this approach achieves a more natural look and smoother topology. **[Topology Comparison: Pattern vs Texture]** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330162457) * * * ### **Case #3. Fixing Small patterns** For garments with small patterns, small patterns may disappear or result in unnatural topology across the entire garment during the optimization. Therefore, before optimization, merging small patterns into nearby larger patterns is strongly recommended. **[Topology Comparison: Before and After Merging]** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330163609) * **How to Merge Small Patterns** 1. Click on the line segments of two patterns you want to merge. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836713753) 2. Right-click and select ‘Merge.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836716057) * * * ### **Case #4. Adding Seam Taping to Skirt Hems** When the skirt pleats are heavily overlapped or touching each other, it can elevate rigging difficulty and cause the pleats to appear incorrect during specific movements. This may lead to clipping issues as the avatar moves. To resolve this, apply the ‘**Seam Taping** ’ function to Skirt hems to relax the pleats and enhance their overall silhouette. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330164377) * **How to apply ‘Seam Taping.’** 1. Click ‘**Edit Pattern** ’ to select the ‘Seam Taping’ option. 2. Check the ‘**Seam Taping** ’ option in the Property Editor. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512853117593)Apply ‘Seam Taping’ to the preferred segments. 3. Modifying the ‘Seam Taping’ Properties. * **Width (mm)** : set the thickness of the ‘Seam Taping.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512853119769) * Physical Property: The higher the value for Bending, the more relaxed the pleats’ appearance becomes. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836722457)Adjusting the value incrementally while checking the pleats’ silhouette for optimal results is recommended rather than starting with a significantly higher Bending value. * * * ### **Case #5. Pleated Skirts Optimization** Pleated garment patterns are usually formed by zigzag overlapping, which can cause some parts of the patterns to be hidden in the overlapped areas. To optimize these garments, it is recommended that the hidden parts of the patterns be deleted, as shown in the image below. * Before Pattern Adjustments ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330167193) * After Pattern Adjustments ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330169753) * * * ### **Case #6. Creating Internal Lines at Joint areas** Reference the example images of ‘avatar joint points’ to create internal lines in the appropriate areas of the garment. These internal lines help define the garment’s topology, improve the edge flow, and enable more natural movement during rigging. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330176153) * * * ### **Case #7. Differences between Physical Garments and Digital Garments** The structural patterns of physical garments and 3D digital garments can vary significantly. While maintaining the original design's essence is crucial, adjustments to detailed elements may be necessary for efficient optimization. For instance, elements like the back of a physical skirt or overlapping patterns on a blouse's sleeves often don't translate directly into digital garments. In such cases, removing unnecessary or hidden patterns is recommended to streamline the workflow. Moreover, unless the textures of the lining and outer fabric are different, the 'Thickness' option comes in handy for effectively simulating thickness, allowing you to eliminate one of the overlapping patterns. When designing digital garments, it's essential to consider the differences between physical and digital patterns to make practical modifications and optimizations. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345814041) * * * ### **Case #8. Refining Garment Silhouettes** When simulating with optimized polygons, you may encounter situations where the garment’s silhouette becomes awkwardly distorted. To address this, the silhouette must be refined and shaped into a more natural form. This process may also involve adjusting the positions of misaligned buttons or trims, resulting in high-quality garments. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345816729)<Before/After Comparison Image: Garment Button Position Adjustment after Mesh Optimization.> Garments are typically designed in an A-pose, with the arms extended outward. However, characters usually assume a standing pose with lowered arms in games. Adjustments should be made before rigging to ensure the garment’s wrinkles appear natural in this standing pose. For instance, wrinkles that occur only in the **A-pose** , such as those at the shoulders of a trench coat, may look unnatural in the standing pose. It is recommended that such wrinkles be removed or smoothed out to maintain a consistent and polished appearance during gameplay. Various methods exist to modify wrinkles, and designers can select the best approach to suit their workflow. The primary goal is to elevate the garment’s quality before rigging, achieving a natural silhouette that integrates seamlessly with the character’s poses. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330185369)<Before/After Comparison Image: Shoulder Wrinkle Adjustment> * * * ### **Case #9. Approaching Garment adjustment based on Avatar Mesh Handling** The process and priorities for modifying digital garments can vary depending on how the avatar mesh is processed. If the avatar mesh is deleted, there is less concern about it protruding through the garment during rigging test motions. However, greater focus is needed to ensure the garment’s overall silhouette remains clean and accurate to the intended design. For instance, if parts of the avatar mesh are visible through the garment, but the silhouette looks natural, and the design intent is well-preserved, modifications might not be necessary. However, adjustments are essential if the silhouette looks indented or distorted, regardless of whether mesh penetrations are present. When the avatar mesh is not deleted, the primary goal is to prevent it from protruding through the garment during rigging tests. After addressing this, further refinements are recommended to maintain a natural silhouette that aligns with the intended design. Defining clear workflows and inspection criteria based on how the avatar mesh is processed can enhance efficiency while maintaining high garment quality. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330187929)<Example images of acceptable garment penetrations when deleting an avatar mesh.> * * * ### **Case #10. Considerations for Button and Trim Optimization** Switching the ‘**Polygon Optimization** ’ type to ‘**Billboard** ’ can be highly beneficial when optimizing the garment accessories such as buttons, trims, and zippers. However, it's crucial to approach this change with care, considering each element's position and purpose. It is generally recommended that garment accessories be used with ‘**Mesh** ’ instead of ‘**Billboard** ’ to better preserve their shape and volume. Accessories worn near the face are especially important, as they often appear in close-up shots and can impact the overall quality. In such cases, working in ‘**Mesh** ’ is required to ensure the shape is not overly distorted. Furthermore, when an accessory plays a significant or defining role in the outfit, it’s recommended to use ‘**Mesh** ’ instead of ‘**Billboard** ’ to preserve its details. On the other hand, switching to ‘**Billboard** ’ can help optimize polygon usage effectively for less visible elements like zipper stoppers or small accessories. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345821849) * * * ### **Case #11. Capping Openings with Pattern Thickness** Openings in a garment are normally sealed with the **Auto Seal** tool, but in certain situations you can achieve the same result by extending the pattern’s **Thickness** instead. Using **Auto Seal** adds internal faces along the new cap, which raises both the polygon count and the overall complexity of the garment’s topology. By contrast, sealing a hole with **Thickness** introduces no extra internal faces, allowing you to preserve the existing polygon budget and mesh layout. Because a Thickness cap leaves no gap between the garment and the avatar, there is little space for ambient‑occlusion shadows to form; the surface can appear flat or even slightly unnatural. For that reason, this method is best reserved for tight‑fitting areas—such as sleeve cuffs or hems—where the garment already sits flush against the body. In these zones the added thickness remains virtually invisible, so you can maintain a clean silhouette while still benefiting from the lighter topology. When sealing holes with Thickness, set the **Extrusion Direction** to **Back** to keep the outer silhouette intact, and apply only as much thickness as needed to cover the opening. This ensures the inside of the garment stays hidden without distorting its overall shape.
```
💡Example image of filling holes using pattern thickness
``` * Trouser hem ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330194713) * Armhole ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345826969) * Neckline ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345829657) ```
Using Thickness to seal openings is generally recommended for tight‑fitting areas that receive little visual attention. However, if Fill Hole is difficult to apply—such as along a complex neckline—or if increasing the polygon count is not feasible, you can seal the opening with Thickness as an exception. ``` * * * ### **Case #12. Creating Layer Offsets with Extrusion Direction** When building a garment, the pattern’s **Extrusion Direction** is set to **Back** by default so the outer silhouette remains unchanged. If you need to add a layered offset, however, you can adjust the extrusion direction to give the pattern additional depth. Using **Forward** for this purpose is not recommended, because it moves the new thickness in the opposite direction of the default Back setting; the two layers no longer meet and the garment can look visibly disconnected. To achieve a clean offset, set the extrusion direction to **Both** and fine‑tune the thickness value until the desired step is visible while the overall silhouette stays intact.
```

``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446314649)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446315801)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512430335385) * * * ### **Case #13. Creating a Natural Collar Fold Using Internal Lines and Fold Angles** As the particle distance increases, it can become difficult to maintain a balanced collar shape. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512430336537) In such cases, you can create a more natural collar form by adding internal lines to the collar pattern. As shown in the image below, insert 2–3 internal lines near the sewing line. These lines help define the garment's topology, resulting in a smoother mesh flow.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446320281) Next, assign appropriate fold angles to the added internal lines in the Property Editor. To achieve a natural folding effect, set the fold angles between **0° and 180°** , bending outward from the collar pattern. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446321433) * * * ### **Case #14. Collar Adjustment and Weight Painting Guide** Please refer to this video. [**[LINK]**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19rpYL-RegyAaqJ3zTPjdiht0FwiUC4OZ/view?usp=sharing) * **Hide Unnecessary Mesh Using the Masking Brush** * Use the Masking Brush to hide any unnecessary mesh that is protruding from the inside or intersecting with the avatar. * **Maintain Proper Distance from the Avatar** Use the Grab Brush to slightly offset the collar so it doesn’t sit too tightly against the avatar’s neck. Leave enough space to avoid mesh penetration during animation. * **Refine the Shape** If the collar shape becomes distorted after adjusting the distance, use the Grab Brush to reshape it naturally. Make sure the silhouette flows smoothly and looks clean. * **Adjust Weights** If the collar intersects or collapses when the neck rotates, use the Smooth Multiple Joint Brush or standard Weight Brush to refine the weight painting and ensure smoother deformation. * **Final Check** Apply the test animation to check if the silhouette stays clean during movement and rotation. Make sure there’s no clipping, collapsing, or sharp deformations.

title: Setting up Unreal Engine & LiveSync plugin
content: Please note that installation process for CLO LiveSync and MD LiveSync is identical. Only the folder names of zip folders are different (CLO LiveSync vs. MD LiveSync). 1\. Install [Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin](https://www.unrealengine.com/marketplace/en-US/product/substance-plugin?sessionInvalidated=true) for a desired Unreal Engine version. 2\. Unzip the downloaded zip folder (CLOLiveSync.zip or MDLiveSync.zip), then install LiveSync to UE 5.x by putting CLOLiveSync folder in the following directory of your Unreal Engine installation. (default directory path: C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.x\Engine\Plugins\Marketplace) This folder is where Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin is located.![Untitled \(5\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775724067481) 3\. [Create a new project](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/creating-a-new-project-in-unreal-engine/), or [open an existing project](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/opening-an-existing-unreal-engine-project/). 4\. Make sure that LiveSync and Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin are enabled in Plugins settings. 5\. In the top toolbar, go to Edit - Project Settings, then locate Platforms - Windows options to find **Targeted RHIs** to set its value to **DirectX 11** or**DirectX 12.** Please note that setting Targeted RHIs to DirectX 12 may cause unexpected graphics driver crashes in Unreal Engine 5 while using LiveSync. DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 can be used in following scenarios: * DirectX 11: using Lumen and not using Path Tracer * DirectX 12: disabling Enable Order Independent Translucency (OIT), and using Path Tracer rather than Lumen * Experimental UE5 features often require DirectX 12. Please note that assets brought to Unreal Editor via LiveSync may not open if the setting bounces between DirectX 11 and DirectX 12. ![2.1.1 dx11 setting.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775724282137) 6\. In the top toolbar, go to Edit > Project Settings, and search ‘transparency’ to locate **Enable Order Independent Translucency** (OIT) option to enable the option. ![Untitled \(6\).png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775683747481) 7\. Restart Unreal Editor. 8\. To launch Live Sync Editor, go to Window > CLO/MD LiveSync Editor.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step installation instructions for CLO LiveSync and MD LiveSync for Unreal Engine, highlighting the identical installation process and essential settings to ensure optimal performance.
